## Public Types (`src/model/mod.rs`)

```rust
/// Classification of a policy requirement's obligation strength.
///
/// Derived from heuristic verb matching against RFC 2119 keywords in
/// `PolicyRequirement.text`. Applied by the WI-33 modality detection
/// enrichment pass (`annotate_modalities`).
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```
/// use forge::model::Modality;
///
/// let m = Modality::Normative;
/// assert_eq!(format!("{m:?}"), "Normative");
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Modality {
    /// Mandatory obligation: triggered by "must", "shall", "will", "required".
    /// Also the default when no modality verb is detected.
    Normative,
    /// Recommendation or optional practice: triggered by "should", "may",
    /// "recommended", "optional".
    Advisory,
}
```

    /// Modality classification for this requirement.
    ///
    /// - `None` until `annotate_modalities` runs (pre-WI-33)
    /// - `Some(Modality::Normative)` for normative requirements (or default)
    /// - `Some(Modality::Advisory)` for advisory requirements
    ///
    /// After `annotate_modalities` completes, all requirements in the
    /// document have `Some(modality)`.
    pub modality: Option<Modality>,
}

## Internal Types (`src/parse/modality.rs`)

```rust
/// Result of modality detection for a single policy requirement.
///
/// Carries the classification plus diagnostic metadata for logging.
/// Not part of the public API — used internally by `annotate_modalities`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ModalityResult {
    /// The detected modality classification.
    pub modality: Modality,
    /// Verb strings matched in the requirement text.
    /// Empty when `is_default` is `true` (no verbs found).
    /// Contains verbs from both categories when `has_conflict` is `true`.
    pub matched_verbs: Vec<String>,
    /// `true` when no modality verb was detected; default (Normative) applied.
    pub is_default: bool,
    /// `true` when both normative and advisory verbs were detected.
    /// Normative classification applied (strongest wins).
    pub has_conflict: bool,
}
```

## Static Patterns (`src/parse/modality.rs`)

```rust
use std::sync::LazyLock;
use regex::Regex;

/// Compiled regex for normative verb detection.
///
/// Matches: must, shall, will, required (case-insensitive, word-boundary-aware).
///
/// # Pattern
/// `(?i)\b(must|shall|will|required)\b`
///
/// # Safety
/// Pattern is static and validated at compile time via tests.
/// Will panic at first use if the pattern is invalid (acceptable: static patterns never fail).
static NORMATIVE_PATTERN: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"(?i)\b(must|shall|will|required)\b")
        .expect("NORMATIVE_PATTERN is a valid static regex")
});

/// Compiled regex for advisory verb detection.
///
/// Matches: should, may, recommended, optional (case-insensitive, word-boundary-aware).
///
/// # Pattern
/// `(?i)\b(should|may|recommended|optional)\b`
///
/// # Safety
/// Pattern is static and validated at compile time via tests.
/// Will panic at first use if the pattern is invalid (acceptable: static patterns never fail).
static ADVISORY_PATTERN: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"(?i)\b(should|may|recommended|optional)\b")
        .expect("ADVISORY_PATTERN is a valid static regex")
});
```

## Public Functions (`src/parse/modality.rs`)

### `detect_modality`

```rust
/// Detect modality for a single policy requirement.
///
/// Scans `requirement.text` against `NORMATIVE_PATTERN` and `ADVISORY_PATTERN`.
/// Returns a `ModalityResult` with the classification and diagnostic metadata.
///
/// Classification rules:
/// 1. Normative verbs only → `Modality::Normative`
/// 2. Advisory verbs only → `Modality::Advisory`
/// 3. Both found (conflict) → `Modality::Normative`, `has_conflict = true`
/// 4. Neither found (default) → `Modality::Normative`, `is_default = true`
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `requirement` - The policy requirement to classify
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```
/// use forge::model::{PolicyRequirement, Modality};
/// use forge::parse::modality::detect_modality;
///
/// let req = PolicyRequirement {
///     text: "Organizations must implement encryption.".into(),
///     // ... other fields
/// #   stable_id: None, source_line: 1, nesting_depth: 0, atom_index: 0,
/// #   parent_text: None, citations: vec![], modality: None,
/// };
/// let result = detect_modality(&req);
/// assert_eq!(result.modality, Modality::Normative);
/// assert!(result.matched_verbs.contains(&"must".to_string()));
/// assert!(!result.is_default);
/// assert!(!result.has_conflict);
/// ```
pub fn detect_modality(requirement: &PolicyRequirement) -> ModalityResult;
```

### `annotate_modalities`

```rust
/// Annotate all requirements in a document with modality classifications.
///
/// Iterates over every `PolicyRequirement` in every section (including nested
/// children), calls `detect_modality` on each, and sets `requirement.modality`.
///
/// Emits `tracing::warn!` for:
/// - Requirements with no modality verb detected (`is_default = true`)
/// - Requirements with conflicting normative/advisory verbs (`has_conflict = true`)
///
/// Emits `tracing::debug!` for matched verbs on every requirement.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `document` - The policy document with atomized requirements (post-WI-7)
///
/// # Returns
/// The same document with all `requirement.modality` fields populated.
///
/// # Errors
/// Currently infallible — modality detection cannot fail (static patterns).
/// Returns `Result` for pipeline consistency with other enrichment passes.
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```
/// use forge::parse::modality::annotate_modalities;
///
/// let annotated = annotate_modalities(document)?;
/// assert!(annotated.sections.iter().all(|s|
///     s.requirements.iter().all(|r| r.modality.is_some())
/// ));
/// ```
pub fn annotate_modalities(document: PolicyDocument) -> Result<PolicyDocument, ForgeError>;
```

## Invariants

1. After `annotate_modalities(doc)` returns `Ok(doc)`, every `PolicyRequirement` in the document has `modality: Some(_)`.
2. `detect_modality` never returns `is_default = true` AND `has_conflict = true` simultaneously (mutually exclusive).
3. `detect_modality` never returns `has_conflict = true` with an Advisory classification (normative always wins on conflict).
4. `NORMATIVE_PATTERN` and `ADVISORY_PATTERN` use only simple alternation — no nested quantifiers, no unbounded repetition (SEC-3).
5. Both patterns are compiled exactly once per process lifetime via `LazyLock` (SEC-4).
